Koi · car-cost ledger · design batch 2 · sheet 12

Reminders & papers

Tell me once, in time, and never again — plus the one page that must not invent a single field
DRAWS    wireframes §9.1 – §9.4 · §10
READS    spec §C7 · §C8 · §D5 · §D6
FIXTURE  §0.6 · today 28 Jul 2026
DATE     2026-08-04
THE PROMISE

A reminder is a date, not a nag

Koi tells you once, at a time you chose, and then stops. Overdue is stated as a fact in attention, never escalated, never re-nagged, never red — being late is information, not a failure.

Milestone anniversaries are off by default (§C7). An app that congratulates you on owning a car for a year is performing enthusiasm at someone who asked for a ledger.

TWO KINDS, ONE LIST
Date-based — ITV, insurance, tax. Fires on a calendar date, with alerts at 60 / 30 / 7 days before. Predictable, and the anchor is a date you can check.
Distance-based — the next oil change at 93.000 km. Has no date until Koi predicts one from your real pace, so it is always phrased in time: "around November at your pace", never as frozen remaining-km.

That phrasing is the whole design of the second kind. 3.760 km to go is true and useless; around November is what a person plans around.

§16 #18 TAKEN AT ITS RECOMMENDATION

The page is "Insurance & papers". Vault stays internal.

"Vault" appears nowhere in §C8's own copy, and the product is already spending one new coinage on lens. Plain language wins the user-facing title; vault stays the route name.

One door, not two. The car page carries a single Care row whose meta does the second row's job — Renews 16 Aug · 3 papers. Two rows to one page is a nav smell.

01 · The list and the detail

Reached from Home's All › and from the car page's Care group — so it is a shared destination, pushed inside whichever tab you came from.

Three groups, and the boundary between the middle two is the same 28 days Home's state machine uses — so what Home calls Coming up and what this list calls Next 28 days can never disagree about which reminders those are.

The distance-based row is the only one with no date: at 95.000 km is the anchor, ≈November is Koi's prediction at 14,7 km/day — and the ≈ says so. It sits in Later because its predicted date is months out, not because of its km.

The Anchor row is what makes the alert schedule checkable. Home's card says only what fires next; this page shows the whole rule and then states plainly that all three alerts have already fired — so an overdue reminder cannot be mistaken for one still counting down.

Snooze moves the date, it does not silence anything — the reminder reappears on the new date and the list re-sorts. Mark done names the date it will create, so a recurring reminder never quietly re-arms itself behind the user's back.

Permission denied is one quiet line, once

Alerts are off. Turn on in iOS Settings ›

Not a banner, not repeated per reminder, not a modal on launch. The reminders themselves still work — they are dates in a ledger, and the list still shows them. Only the notification is missing, so only the notification is mentioned.

The builder is a sheet, and it asks two questions

On a date At a distance
WhatITV
When16 Jul 2027
Repeatsevery 12 months

The kind chips come first because they change which fields follow — a date picker or a km target, never both. Alerts default to 60/30/7 and are not asked about; a reminder should be creatable in four taps.

Swap retires the reminders it must

When a subscription car is swapped, date-based reminders carry over to the new car — an ITV date belongs to the plan's lineage. Distance-based ones retire: "oil at 95.000 km" is meaningless on a car with a different odometer, and silently re-anchoring it would invent a target the user never set.

Empty, and honest about which empty

No reminders at all → "Nothing scheduled. Add the ITV date or a service target." — it names the two a driver actually has.

All clear → "Nothing due in the next few weeks." The list still shows the Later group, because "quiet" is not "empty" and the user came here to check.

02 · Insurance & papers

Facts only. Gaps say not on file — this is the one page whose entire rule is never to invent a field.

Photos are downscaled and stripped of location data before they are saved.

Papers carry kind and title only. No "Added 12 Jun", no file size, no page count — the data model has none of those, and inventing them on the one page whose rule is never to invent would be the worst possible place to start.

The renewal card appears at ≤30 days out. After the date its first line becomes "Cover ran to 16 Aug. Most policies roll over automatically." — past tense, same three answers, still no alarm.

AND WHEN A POLICY HAS GAPS
Línea Directa
Policynot on file

Premium305,00 €
vs last yearfirst year on file

No renewal card without a date to renew on — Koi will not guess one. vs last year reads first year on file, never +0,00 €.

Two different absences, drawn together because they are constantly confused. No policy at all is a missing door — it needs an action. A policy with gaps is a filled row that says not on file — it needs nothing but honesty. Collapsing them would either hide the door or nag about optional fields.

The second sentence exists because the Golf does have a policy: with two cars in the garage, "no insurance on file" invites the assumption that Koi will reuse the other one. It says plainly that it will not.

"It lapsed" is the answer §C8 was missing

The spec offered only Renewed and Switched insurer — so a driver whose cover actually lapsed could record it only as a fake renewal, corrupting the premium trend and re-arming a reminder for a policy that no longer exists.

The third button clears the valid-until date, retires the renewal reminder, and leaves the premium history intact. A ledger has to be able to record the bad outcome.

One form, three doors

The header pencil, Switched insurer, and Add your policy all open the same policy form, prefilled to whatever exists. Three entry points, one surface — the same rule that stops the odometer sheet from being reimplemented per screen.

Renewed unfolds; it does not push

It reveals one inline premium field — "Leave it empty if the price didn't change." — then rolls the dates forward a year and re-arms the reminder. The trend label stays strictly "vs last year" even after switching insurer, because that phrasing is true either way.

Where the renewal shows up elsewhere

Recording a renewal writes a milestone into History — Insurance renewed · Mapfre · 412,00 € · +14 € vs last year, with no amount column, because a premium is a fact and not a July charge. That row's glance sheet points back to this page.

Sheet 12 of batch 2. One sheet left: 13 onboarding — first run, the first car, the first fill. Note that notification scheduling is not installed in the build (expo-notifications is not a dependency), so every alert line on this sheet is design intent, not current behaviour.
